protocol.name: cupertino_shell_v1

description.summary: private protocol between the Cupertino server and its shell processes

protocol.description: Roles the server gives only to the shell processes it starts (menu bar, dock, window manager, session observer). Applications use cupertino_app_effects_v1 instead. The protocol is unstable until phase 1 of ends: interfaces may change without a version bump until then.

interface.name: cupertino_shell_v1

description.summary: shell services of the server

interface.description: Global singleton, offered only to the processes the server started for a shell role, on a connection of their own. Each request needs the role it creates: a connection that holds other roles, or none, gets the permission error. Version 2 adds the display options of the session object, version 3 the screen capture state of the menu bar object. Version 5 moves the backdrops and the title bar style of application windows to the public cupertino_app_effects_v1 protocol, which any client may use, and removes their requests here. Version 6 adds the session_action request of the menu bar object, version 7 the lock_requested event of the session object, version 8 the session_agent event of the menu bar object, version 9 the log_out_requested event of the session object, version 10 the window list, the shortcuts and the further window commands of the menu bar object, version 11 its edit request, version 12 its engage_help event, version 13 its force_quit_app request, version 14 its backdrop_luminance event, version 15 its window_controls event, version 16 its window_full_screen event, version 17 the window_icon event of the dock object, version 18 its engage event, version 19 its app_resident event, version 20 the activate_app request and app_activation event of the session object, version 21 the backdrop_bands event of the menu bar object. An object this global creates has the version the global was bound at, so the since of each message of those objects is the shell version that added it.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: unbind the shell global

request.description: Objects created through this global stay valid.

entry.name: role
entry.summary: the surface is not a layer surface of that output, already has a role, or the output already has this role holder

entry.name: permission
entry.summary: the connection does not hold the role the request needs

request.name: get_menu_bar

description.summary: make a layer surface the menu bar of an output

request.description: Gives the menu-bar role to a layer surface anchored to the top edge of the output. The server owns the bar's presentation as on the design: it reserves the bar's height in the output's usable area (the client sets an exclusive zone of 0), dims the bar of an inactive output, hides it in full screen or by policy and reveals it when the pointer dwells at the top edge, by moving and fading the surface. The client draws the bar content and opens its menus as popups of this surface.

request.name: get_dock

description.summary: make a layer surface the dock of an output

request.description: Gives the dock role to a layer surface on that output. Unlike the menu bar, the client owns the dock's presentation: tile layout, magnification, bounces, auto-hide and its reserved area (through the layer surface's exclusive zone). The server tells it which windows exist and takes its activation requests. The area of the surface's committed backdrops is the dock's rectangle for the server, for example the origin of windows entering the overview, so the surface may be larger than the bar. Posts the role error when the surface is not a layer surface of that output, already has a role, or the output already has a dock.

request.name: get_session

description.summary: follow the appearance and lock state of the session

request.description: Creates an observer of the session. It has no surface or role, so a client may create any number of them. The server sends the current state right after the object is created and again on every change.

request.name: get_window_manager

description.summary: arrange the windows of an output

request.description: Makes the client the window manager of the output: the process that owns the stage policy (which windows share the stage, the strip of recent groups). It needs no surface. Posts the role error when the output is gone or already has a window manager.

interface.name: cupertino_window_manager_v1

description.summary: the window manager of one output

interface.description:
Events describe the windows the client arranges and the input meant for it. They come in groups ended by a done event; the client applies a group at once. The first group, sent right after the object is created, has the usable area and every arranged window. Window ids are the server's, the same as the dock's.
The arranged windows are the mapped, unminimized top-level windows without a parent on the output's current workspace (or on every workspace), of applications that are not hidden.
The client decides where each arranged window rests; the server keeps the frame clock: it animates every window from where it is drawn to its committed placement, draws strip windows as live thumbnails scaled into their rectangle, keeps strip and hidden windows out of pointer hit testing and reports presses on strip windows. A window starts on the stage and returns to it when it leaves the arranged set. When the object is destroyed, also when the client dies, every window is drawn and hit at its own frame again at once.

request.name: destroy

description.summary: stop arranging the output's windows

request.description: Every window returns to the stage at once.

event.name: usable_area

description.summary: the area windows may use

event.description: The output minus the menu bar and the reserved layer zones, in global logical coordinates. Sent in the first group and on every change.

entry.name: active
entry.summary: the key window of the session

event.name: window

description.summary: an arranged window appeared or changed

event.description: Application id (the desktop entry id when known), frame in global logical coordinates and state of a window. Sent when the window joins the arranged set and again whenever one of these changes.

event.name: window_closed

description.summary: a window left the arranged set

event.description: It closed, was minimized, moved to another output or workspace, or its application was hidden. Its placement is dropped.

event.name: toggle_stage

description.summary: the stage shortcut was pressed

event.description: Turn the stage on when it is off and off when it is on.

event.name: strip_pressed

description.summary: the pointer pressed a strip window

event.description: The left button went down on the thumbnail of this window, with nothing of the server's or another client's above it. The press reaches no client.

description.summary: end of a group of events

entry.name: stage
entry.summary: at the window's own frame

entry.name: strip
entry.summary: a thumbnail at the given rectangle

entry.name: hidden
entry.summary: not drawn

request.name: set_placement

description.summary: where a window rests

request.description: Pending until commit. The rectangle, in global logical coordinates, is read only for the strip placement. An id that is not an arranged window is ignored at commit: the window may have just closed.

request.name: commit

description.summary: apply the pending placements together

request.description: Every window whose placement changed starts its animation in the same frame, so a swap of the stage and the strip moves as one.

request.name: activate_window

description.summary: focus and raise a window

request.description: As a click on it does. An id that is no longer a window is ignored.

entry.name: invalid_placement
entry.summary: not an entry of the placement enum, or a strip rectangle without area

interface.name: cupertino_session_v1

description.summary: appearance, display options and lock state of the session

interface.description: The state every shell process follows. Right after the object is created the server sends appearance, then display_options (version 2), then locked or unlocked. Later events say what changed; an event is complete by itself and is not part of a group. The server draws the lock screen's surfaces on its own: a shell process needs to react to locked only by closing transient interface it owns (menus, panels), and it keeps its surfaces.

description.summary: stop observing the session

event.name: appearance

description.summary: the session's appearance

event.description: 1 for the dark appearance, 0 for the light one. The client draws again with it, for example from the colours of its materials and palettes. The materials of the client's backdrops follow the appearance in the server and need no request.

entry.name: reduce_motion
entry.summary: replace spatial transitions with fades

entry.name: reduce_transparency
entry.summary: draw materials opaque

entry.name: increase_contrast
entry.summary: draw with the high-contrast colours

entry.name: differentiate_without_color
entry.summary: do not carry state by colour alone

event.name: display_options

description.summary: the accessibility display options of the session

event.description: The options that are on. The client draws again with them: with reduce_motion it fades what it would slide, scale or magnify; with reduce_transparency and increase_contrast it picks its opaque and high-contrast palettes. The materials of the client's backdrops follow the options in the server and need no request. Bits the client does not know are reserved and stay 0.

event.name: locked

description.summary: the session is locked

event.description: Sent as soon as the server hides the session for the lock, before the lock screen has its first frame. The session stays locked until unlocked, also while the client that took the lock is gone.

description.summary: the session is unlocked

event.name: lock_requested

description.summary: the server asks the lock screen to lock the session

event.description: Sent only to the connection that holds the session lock role, for the lock shortcut, the idle lock and the menu: the client locks as if it had been asked on its own control interface. It is the server's private way to the lock screen, which a process on the session bus cannot take over. explicit is 1 when the person asked for it (the lock shortcut) and 0 when the display slept or the machine is going to sleep.

event.name: log_out_requested

description.summary: the server asks the login process to ask whether to log out

event.description: Sent only to the connection that holds the session lock role, for the log out shortcut and the session menu: the client shows its log out confirmation as if it had been asked on its own control interface, which a process on the session bus cannot take over.

entry.name: activated
entry.summary: the application's windows were brought forward

entry.name: resident
entry.summary: a process of the application runs but shows no window

entry.name: not_running
entry.summary: no process of the application runs

request.name: activate_app

description.summary: bring a running application forward by its desktop file ID

request.description: Brings the application of the desktop file ID desktop_id (with or without the .desktop suffix) forward as the dock's activate_app does, when it shows a window: its frontmost window takes the focus, a minimised one is restored when it has no other, and a hidden application is shown. An application matches when its application id is the desktop file ID, or when the server's desktop entry for its application id has that ID; both compare without regard to case. The server answers with app_activation and the same serial, at once. It starts nothing: the client launches the application itself when the answer is not activated. Needs the Session role, checked on every request: a connection that no longer holds it gets the permission error and nothing is done.

arg.name: serial
arg.summary: chosen by the client, returned in app_activation

event.name: app_activation

description.summary: what activate_app found

event.description: The answer to the activate_app request with this serial: activated when the application showed a window and was brought forward; resident when a process of it is connected after showing a window but shows none now (the client may ask that process for a window); not_running otherwise.

interface.name: cupertino_menu_bar_v1

description.summary: the menu bar of one output

interface.description: Events describe the active application and the menus its active window exports. They come in groups ended by a done event; the client applies a group at once. The first group is sent right after the object is created; from version 3 a group with screen_capture follows it, from version 10 a group with the shortcuts, from version 14 to 20 a group with backdrop_luminance once the server knows it, and from version 21 a group with backdrop_bands in its place.

description.summary: give up the menu-bar role

event.name: active_app

description.summary: the active application changed

event.description: Application id (the desktop entry id when known) and title of the active window; both are empty when no window is active. Each is cut to at most 1024 bytes at a UTF-8 character boundary.

description.summary: the active window exports no menu

event.name: menu_dbusmenu

description.summary: the active window exports a DBusMenu tree

event.description: Announced by the window through the application menu address protocol.

event.name: menu_gtk

description.summary: the active window exports GMenuModel menus

event.description: Announced by the window through the toolkit shell protocol. An empty string is an absent path.

event.name: window_state

description.summary: state of the active window for the window menu

event.description: Whether the active window can zoom, its workspace (1-based, 0 for none) and the number of workspaces of the output.

entry.name: active
entry.summary: the active window

event.name: app_window

description.summary: a window of the active application, for the window list

event.description: One event per toplevel of the active application, in stacking order from the top, at most 1000, in every group that has window_state. The list is complete in each such group and replaces the last one; no event means the application has no window. id is the server's window id (the dock's), stable for the window's lifetime and never reused within a session. title is cut to at most 1024 bytes at a UTF-8 character boundary.

event.name: engage

description.summary: the menu-bar shortcut was pressed

event.description: Focus the first menu title of this bar for keyboard navigation. The bar takes the keyboard by asking for exclusive keyboard interactivity and lets go when navigation ends. Sent in a group of its own, ended by done.

event.name: screen_capture

description.summary: whether the screen is being captured

event.description: 1 while a screen or window capture session runs (ext-image-copy-capture-v1), 0 otherwise. The bar shows the screen capture indicator while it is 1. Sent in a group of its own, ended by done, after the first group and whenever it changes.

entry.name: none
entry.summary: no session agent runs: nothing on the bus is the agent

entry.name: process
entry.summary: the owner of the agent's bus name is the agent when it is the process named by pid

entry.name: any
entry.summary: a development run: whoever owns the agent's bus name is the agent

event.name: session_agent

description.summary: which process is the session agent

event.description: Names the process that may answer as the session agent (`org.cupertino.Login1`): the server started it. The bar takes the session menu's state (the user name and what the machine allows) only from the owner of that bus name when it is this process, so a client that took the name first cannot write the menu. pid is 0 unless trust is process. Sent in a group of its own, ended by done, after the first group and whenever it changes.

event.name: shortcut

description.summary: the chord the server binds to an action

event.description: The physical chord that runs the action, in the shortcut file's syntax (modifiers in the order Ctrl, Alt, Shift, Super, then the key name, joined by "+"); empty when nothing is bound. One event per bound_action entry of the object's version, in a group of its own ended by done, after the first group and whenever the bindings or the modifier profile change.

entry.name: super
entry.summary: the cupertino profile: Super is the command key

entry.name: ctrl
entry.summary: the classic-pc profile: Ctrl is the command key

event.name: primary_modifier

description.summary: the physical key of the primary modifier

event.description: Which key the active modifier profile makes the primary modifier, for the chords the bar shows for applications' own items. Sent in the shortcut group.

description.summary: end of a group of events

event.name: engage_help

description.summary: the help search shortcut was pressed

event.description: Open this bar's Help menu with its search field focused, taking the keyboard as for engage. Sent in a group of its own, ended by done, to the bar of the output with the active window (else the output under the pointer), like engage. Never sent while the session is locked or a lock is pending.

event.name: backdrop_luminance

description.summary: how light the wallpaper under the bar is

event.description: The perceptual lightness (CIE L*/100) of the mean colour of the output's wallpaper under the bar's strip, in thousandths: 0 black, 1000 white. Sent to a bar of version 14 to 20 (a later bar gets backdrop_bands), in a group of its own, ended by done, once the server knows it: after the first groups, and again when it moves by more than 10. A server that has no measure sends nothing, and the bar keeps the palette of the appearance. Once sent, a measure is never withdrawn: when the wallpaper image goes, the one drawn in its place is measured. Only the server's own wallpaper image is measured; nothing of a window or another client is sampled.

event.name: backdrop_bands

description.summary: the colour of the wallpaper under the bar, across it

event.description: The mean colour of the output's wallpaper under the bar's strip, in bands of equal width from the output's left edge to its right: for each band, the mean of the encoded sRGB red, green and blue of its pixels, each a little-endian 16-bit value from 0 (none) to 65535 (full), so three values per band and at most 256 bands. The bar averages the bands under an item, or all of them for the whole strip, and takes the relative luminance of that colour. Sent to a bar of version 21 or later in place of backdrop_luminance, in a group of its own ended by done, once the server knows it and again when any band changes. A server that has no measure sends nothing; once sent, a measure is never withdrawn. Only the server's own wallpaper image is measured; nothing of a window or another client is sampled.

entry.name: minimize
entry.summary: the Window menu's Minimize

entry.name: zoom
entry.summary: the Window menu's Zoom

event.name: window_controls

description.summary: the controls of the active window that are enabled

event.description: The controls of the active window that are enabled: those its client did not disable through cupertino_app_effects_v1.set_disabled_controls, and zoom only while the window is resizable. Sent in every group that has window_state. window_state's can_zoom keeps meaning that zoom is enabled, for bars older than version 15. Until the server sends it, both controls are enabled.

event.name: window_full_screen

description.summary: whether the active window is in full screen

event.description: Whether the active window is in full screen (1) or not (0). Sent in every group that has window_state. A window in full screen can always be taken out of it, whatever its controls, so a bar offers leaving full screen then even where window_controls has zoom disabled. Until the server sends it, the window is taken as not in full screen.

request.name: set_menu_open

description.summary: a menu of this bar is open or closed

request.description: While a menu is open the server keeps the bar revealed.

entry.name: hide_app
entry.summary: hide the active application

entry.name: hide_others
entry.summary: hide every other application

entry.name: show_all
entry.summary: show all hidden applications

entry.name: quit_app
entry.summary: close every window of the active application

entry.name: minimize
entry.summary: minimize the active window

entry.name: zoom
entry.summary: zoom the active window

entry.name: close
entry.summary: close the active window

entry.name: toggle_fullscreen
entry.summary: enter or leave full screen with the active window

entry.name: tile_left
entry.summary: tile the active window to the left half of its output

entry.name: tile_right
entry.summary: tile the active window to the right half of its output

entry.name: tile_fill
entry.summary: make the active window fill its output's usable area

entry.name: bring_all_to_front
entry.summary: raise every window of the active application, keeping their order and the focus

entry.name: cascade_all
entry.summary: bring_all_to_front, and cascade the windows 24 pt apart from the active one

entry.name: minimize_all
entry.summary: minimize every window of the active application

entry.name: zoom_all
entry.summary: zoom every window of the active application that can zoom

entry.name: force_quit_dialog
entry.summary: open the force quit dialog

request.name: window_command

description.summary: run a window-management command of the fallback menus

request.description: Acts on the active application or window at the time the server handles the request.

entry.name: invalid_command
entry.summary: the window_command value is not an entry of the command enum

entry.name: invalid_session_action
entry.summary: the session_action value is not an entry of the session_action enum

entry.name: invalid_edit_action
entry.summary: the edit value is not an entry of the edit_action enum

request.name: move_to_workspace

description.summary: move the active window to a workspace of its output

request.description: 1-based workspace index.

entry.name: sleep
entry.summary: put the computer to sleep without asking

entry.name: restart
entry.summary: ask whether to restart

entry.name: shut_down
entry.summary: ask whether to shut down

entry.name: lock
entry.summary: lock the session on the person's request

entry.name: log_out
entry.summary: ask whether to log out

entry.name: switch_user
entry.summary: lock the session and show the login window

entry.name: refresh_capabilities
entry.summary: read again what the session menu may offer

request.name: session_action

description.summary: an entry of the session menu was chosen

request.description: The server asks the session agent on the menu bar's behalf: the agent answers only the server and the process itself, so a shell process cannot reach it directly. The result shows in the agent's properties.

request.name: activate_window

description.summary: a row of the window list was chosen

request.description: Show the window: unminimize it, switch to its workspace, raise and focus it. An id that names no window of the active application when the request arrives is ignored, since the list can change in the meantime. The request is also ignored while the session is locked.

request.name: edit

description.summary: an item of the Edit menu was chosen

request.description:
The server sends the key chord of the action to the key window, as if it was typed there.
The request counts only while a popup of this menu bar holds the popup grab when it arrives; at any other time it is ignored. The target is the key window at that moment, and only when it is the xdg toplevel of an application: never an X11 window, a lock surface, the greeter, a layer surface or a surface of a shell process. Nothing is sent, and the request is ignored without an error, while the session is locked or a lock is pending, while the overview or the application switcher is open, or while another grab holds the pointer or the keyboard.
The server keeps one edit; a newer request replaces it. It sends the edit once, on the first change of keyboard focus after the popup grab ends, and only when that change gives the keyboard to the target window and comes within 500 ms of the request's arrival. Any other first focus, or no focus change within 500 ms, drops the edit. Every condition above is checked again right before the chord is sent.
The chord depends on the application. A terminal (an application id in the server's list of terminals, the list its keyboard rewrite reads) gets only copy and paste, as Shift+Ctrl+c and Shift+Ctrl+v, and nothing for the other actions. A first-party application (an id that starts with "cupertino-"), or an application the keyboard rewrite is off for, gets the primary modifier of the modifier profile (Super under cupertino, Ctrl under classic-pc) with z for undo, Shift and z for redo, and x, c, v and a for cut, copy, paste and select all. Any other application gets the same keys with Ctrl, whatever the profile: so a terminal missing from the list gets Ctrl+c on copy, as the keyboard rewrite gives it for Super+c.
The client is told the chord's modifiers; then the key that types the letter in the active layout (else the key the shortcuts' Latin fallback maps to it) is pressed and released at once, and the client is told the real modifiers again. The key never repeats and never runs a shortcut of the server. An action value outside edit_action is the error invalid_edit_action.

request.name: force_quit_app

description.summary: force quit the active application, named as the bar's label shows it

request.description:
The alternate of the Force Quit item, chosen with Alt held: the choice that names the application is the confirmation. app_id is the active application's id as the bar last got it in active_app. The server ends the application only if app_id equals the id of the active application when it handles the request, the same way as the dock's force_quit_app: an application that does not answer its pings is killed at once (SIGKILL); any other gets a close request for each of its windows and SIGTERM, and SIGKILL three seconds later if a process is still there.
Any other app_id (the active application changed in the meantime, or there is none), an app_id longer than 255 bytes, and every request while the session is locked or a lock is pending, is ignored without an error. There is no reply; the application's windows closing is the result.

interface.name: cupertino_dock_v1

description.summary: the dock of one output

interface.description:
Events describe the windows of the session and the application switcher. They come in groups ended by a done event; the client applies a group at once. The first group, sent right after the object is created, lists every window; while a switch is under way, the switcher as it stands follows in a group of its own. Window ids are the server's, stable for a window's lifetime and never reused within a session.
The server owns the switcher's keys and its choice: it opens on the switch chord, steps on its keys, commits the selected application when the modifier is released and cancels on Escape, with or without a dock. One dock draws the panel (after its show delay and with its fade), on the output switcher_output names, and reports what the pointer did on it: the entry it picked, a release on an entry (switcher_activate) or elsewhere on the panel (switcher_cancel). The panel is a layer surface of namespace cupertino-dock-switcher; a press anywhere else cancels the switch when it is released.
The overview (all windows, or one application's) is shared the same way: the server owns its transition, the windows' frames and their animation, and closes it on Escape, on a workspace switch and when the dock goes away; the dock lays the windows out (overview_frame), draws the workspaces bar, the highlight and the titles, and sends what the pointer and the keys picked. Hot corners and touchpad gestures are detected by the server and mapped to their action by the dock (hot_corner, gesture, run_action). Overview coordinates are the output's logical coordinates (origin at the output's top-left corner).

description.summary: give up the dock role

entry.name: active
entry.summary: the key window of the session

event.name: window

description.summary: a window appeared or changed

event.description: Application id (the desktop entry id when known), title and state of a window. Sent when the window is mapped and again whenever one of these changes. The application id and the title are each cut to at most 1024 bytes at a UTF-8 character boundary.

description.summary: a window went away

event.name: launching

description.summary: the server started an application

event.description: Sent when the server itself starts a program (a shortcut or a spawned command), so the dock can bounce its tile until a window of that application appears.

event.name: toggle_auto_hide

description.summary: the auto-hide shortcut was pressed

event.description: Turn the dock's auto-hide on when it is off and off when it is on. The dock updates its exclusive zone to match.

event.name: toggle_app_grid

description.summary: the application grid action was triggered (no longer sent)

event.description: The server no longer sends this event: the app-grid action opens the launcher's application browser, which the server asks for on the session bus. A dock that maps a hot corner or gesture to that action sends it back with run_action. The event stays so that existing docks keep binding; a dock that gets it may ignore it.

event.name: switcher_output

description.summary: the output the switcher's panel goes on

event.description: Starts every switcher group, before its switcher_entry events: the output the panel is drawn on, the one under the pointer when the switch opened. Only one dock gets the switcher groups: the dock of that output, else another one. When the client has not bound that output, the server names the dock's own output.

event.name: switcher_entry

description.summary: an entry of the application switcher

event.description: One application of the switcher's list, most recently used first. The entries sent since the last done, up to the switcher_changed that ends them, are the whole list; they replace any earlier one.

event.name: switcher_changed

description.summary: the application switcher opened or its selection moved

event.description: Closes the list of switcher_entry events before it in the group and selects one of them (0-based). The list is never empty and the index is inside it. Sent when the switcher opens, on every step and on every switcher_select that moved the selection, each time with the whole list again. A dock that binds while a switch is under way gets it right after its first group, in a group of its own.

event.name: switcher_closed

description.summary: the application switcher is gone

event.description: The switch ended. When committed is 1 the selected application was activated and the panel fades out; when 0 it was cancelled and the panel disappears at once. Sent after the last switcher_changed of the switch.

entry.name: all
entry.summary: every window of the current workspace, with the workspaces bar

entry.name: app
entry.summary: the windows of one application, minimized ones in a lower row

event.name: overview_window

description.summary: a window of the open overview

event.description: One window the overview shows, with its frame on the desktop (for a minimized window: its frame before it minimized). The windows sent since the last done, up to the overview_changed that ends them, are the whole set; they replace any earlier one. Their ids are those of the window events.

event.name: overview_workspace

description.summary: a workspace of the output

event.description: One workspace of the dock's output, in order; current is 1 for the one on screen. Sent in the same group as the overview_window events and closed by the same overview_changed. Workspace ids are the server's, stable for a workspace's lifetime.

event.name: overview_changed

description.summary: the overview opened or its contents changed

event.description: Closes the overview_window and overview_workspace lists before it in the group. Sent when the overview opens on the dock's output, whenever its window set or the workspaces change while it is open, and to a dock that binds while it is open. app_id is the application of the app mode, empty in the all mode. The rectangle is the area the windows are laid out in: the output minus the menu bar and the layer-shell exclusive zones. The dock answers with one overview_frame per window; until it does, a window stays at its desktop frame.

event.name: overview_closed

description.summary: the overview is leaving

event.description: The server started the close transition: the windows return to their desktop frames. The dock removes its chrome. Sent after a selection, Escape, a workspace switch or an overview_close, and when the overview ends for any other reason.

event.name: hot_corner

description.summary: the pointer rested in a corner of the dock's output

event.description: The pointer dwelt in the corner for the configured time. The dock maps the corner to its action (its own settings) and carries it out, by run_action for the server's actions.

entry.name: swipe_up
entry.summary: a three- or four-finger swipe up

entry.name: swipe_down
entry.summary: a three- or four-finger swipe down

entry.name: pinch
entry.summary: a four-finger pinch in

entry.name: spread
entry.summary: a four-finger spread

event.name: gesture

description.summary: a touchpad gesture committed on the dock's output

event.description: The server's recognizer committed a gesture that is not the workspace swipe (which the server carries out itself). The dock maps it to its action as for hot_corner.

event.name: attention

description.summary: an application asks for attention

event.name: unresponsive

description.summary: an application stopped or resumed answering

event.description: The server pings every client that owns a window; a client that does not answer for two seconds is unresponsive until it does. State 1 says the application stopped answering, 0 that it answers again. The dock marks the application "Not Responding" in its menu and the switcher, and in the Force Quit dialog. Sent to every dock when it changes; right after the object is created, one event per application that is unresponsive then.

event.name: force_quit_dialog

description.summary: the Force Quit shortcut was pressed

event.description: The dock opens its Force Quit Applications dialog, listing the running applications with the unresponsive ones marked, or closes it when it is open. Quitting is force_quit_app, sent only after the person confirmed.

event.name: window_icon

description.summary: the icon a window set for itself

event.description:
The icon the window set with xdg_toplevel_icon_v1, as the server copied it when the window committed it. Sent after the window's window event in the same group when the window has an icon as it maps, and again whenever the window commits a different one, also when it removes its icon. The dock shows it for an application whose desktop entry names no icon.
name is a key into the icon theme, empty for none. It is at most 255 bytes and never holds a slash, two dots in a row or a NUL; the dock never opens it as a path.
size is the side of the square image in pixels, 0 for none. pixels is a sealed file of exactly size * size * 4 bytes: wl_shm argb8888 (premultiplied alpha, little-endian), rows packed. The server copies the largest square image of at most 512 pixels a side. When size is 0 the file is empty.

event.name: engage

description.summary: the Focus Dock shortcut was pressed

event.description: Focus the first tile of the dock for keyboard navigation. The dock takes the keyboard by asking for exclusive keyboard interactivity on its surface and lets go when navigation ends. Sent to the dock of the output under the pointer, else the first dock, in a group of its own ended by done; never while the session is locked or a lock is pending.

event.name: app_resident

description.summary: whether an application's process still runs

event.description: An application is resident while a client of it that showed a window of that application is still connected, with or without windows now: closing its last window does not end it, its process exiting (or its connection closing) does. The first group lists every resident application with resident 1; later groups send a change of either kind, after the window events of the same group. The server's own connections, the shell processes and the X11 bridge (one connection for the windows of every X11 application) are never applications. The application id is cut like the window event's.

arg.name: resident
arg.summary: 1 while resident, 0 once it is no longer

description.summary: end of a group of events

request.name: force_quit_app

description.summary: quit an application at the person's request

request.description: Ends the application after the person confirmed in the Force Quit dialog. An application that does not answer its pings is killed at once (SIGKILL). Any other gets a close request for each of its windows and SIGTERM, and SIGKILL three seconds later if a process is still there. Unknown application ids are ignored: the application may have just quit. There is no reply; the application's windows closing is the result.

request.name: activate_app

description.summary: bring an application forward

request.description: Raises the application's windows on their workspaces and focuses the frontmost, as a click on a running application's tile does. Unknown application ids are ignored: the application may have just quit.

request.name: restore_window

description.summary: restore a minimized window

request.description: Unminimizes the window, animating it out of its tile's rectangle (surface-local). An id that is no longer a minimized window is ignored: it may have just closed or been restored.

request.name: set_minimize_target

description.summary: where a window minimizes to

request.description: The rectangle, in surface-local coordinates, of the slot a newly minimized window's tile takes; the server animates minimizing windows into it. Double-buffered, applied on the next wl_surface.commit. Until one is set, windows minimize without a target.

request.name: switcher_select

description.summary: the pointer picked an entry of the switcher

request.description: Selects entry index of the open switcher, as the pointer hovering over or pressing the entry's tile does; the commit stays with the server's keys. An index outside the list, or a request while no switcher is open, is ignored: the list may have just changed. The server answers with switcher_changed when the selection moved.

request.name: overview_frame

description.summary: where a window of the overview goes

request.description: The frame the window takes in the open overview; the server animates it there (and back to its desktop frame on close). A new frame for a window that has one moves it with the reflow spring. An id that is not in the overview, or a request while none is open, is ignored: the set may have just changed.

request.name: overview_select

description.summary: a window was picked in the overview

request.description: Leaves the overview and activates the window (a minimized one is restored). Ignored for an id that is not in the overview.

description.summary: leave the overview without a pick

request.name: switch_workspace

description.summary: go to a workspace of the dock's output

request.description: Switches the output to the workspace, leaving an open overview first. An unknown id is ignored: the workspace may have just been removed.

description.summary: append a workspace to the dock's output

request.name: remove_workspace

description.summary: remove a workspace of the dock's output

request.description: Its windows move to the previous (else the next) workspace. The last regular workspace, a full-screen one and an unknown id are ignored.

request.name: move_workspace

description.summary: reorder a workspace of the dock's output

request.description: Moves the workspace to position index (0-based) among the output's workspaces; an index past the end moves it last. A full-screen workspace and an unknown id are ignored.

request.name: run_action

description.summary: run a named compositor action

request.description: Runs the action as the shortcut bound to it would (the names of the shortcut file: overview, app-overview, show-desktop, launcher, control-panel, notification-center, lock, ...), for the output under the pointer. An unknown name is logged and ignored.

entry.name: show_windows
entry.summary: open the application overview of the application

entry.name: hide
entry.summary: hide the application's windows

entry.name: quit
entry.summary: ask every window of the application to close

request.name: app_command

description.summary: a command of a tile's context menu

request.description: Carries out the command for the application. Unknown application ids are ignored: the application may have just quit.

request.name: switcher_activate

description.summary: the pointer was released on an entry of the switcher

request.description: Selects entry index of the open switcher and commits it, as releasing the modifier would. An index outside the list, or a request while no switcher is open, is ignored.

request.name: switcher_cancel

description.summary: the pointer was released on the panel off the entries

request.description: Ends the open switch without activating anything; ignored while no switcher is open.
